name: Spaghetti aglio e olio
description: Garlic and chilli gently bloomed in olive oil, then tossed through pasta. Simple, garlicky and a little hot, with no sauce to hide behind.
familiarity_bridge: Like a tadka: aromatics bloomed in hot oil and carried through the dish.
verdict: Worth a try if you enjoy garlic and chilli.
acquired_taste: An approachable first pasta; the garlic is the main event.
how_to_eat: Twirl a small amount with your fork.
Use bread to gather any garlicky oil.
Adjust chilli at the table if offered.
pairing: Bread is good for the garlicky oil; try sparkling water or a light white wine.

taste_bridges.indian: Like a tadka: garlic and chilli bloomed in hot oil, then tossed through the pasta.

name: Spaghetti alla carbonara
description: A glossy sauce made with egg, aged cheese, black pepper and cured pork cheek. Traditional Roman carbonara has no cream.
familiarity_bridge: Rich and peppery, not chilli-spicy; the egg and cheese make it silky.
verdict: Worth a try for you if you eat pork.
acquired_taste: Often an easy first-timer favorite if pork and rich sauces work for you.
how_to_eat: Twirl a small amount against the side of the plate.
Eat while hot so the sauce stays silky.
You can ask for extra cheese if you like.

order_phrases.text: Senza carne di maiale, per favore

pairing: A crisp white wine or sparkling water balances the richness.

name: Spaghetti alla puttanesca
description: A punchy tomato sauce with olives, capers, garlic and often anchovy. Salty, savory and briny.
familiarity_bridge: A bold, tangy tomato base with salty preserved ingredients.
verdict: Try it if you like olives and bold savory flavors.
acquired_taste: Many first-timers find it strong at first; the salty, briny flavor can grow on you.
how_to_eat: Twirl a small amount to try the sauce first.
Take a sip of water between bites if the salt builds.
Ask whether the sauce contains anchovy if you avoid fish.
pairing: Bread helps with the salty sauce; sparkling water or a light red wine works well.

name: Tonnarelli cacio e pepe
description: A Roman pasta of aged sheep's cheese and black pepper, emulsified into a creamy sauce without cream.
familiarity_bridge: Peppery and cheesy, like the warmth of pepper in a dry curry, without the spice mix.
verdict: A good first Roman pasta if you enjoy cheese and pepper.
acquired_taste: Usually approachable; the sheep's cheese can taste sharper than expected.
how_to_eat: Twirl a small amount while the sauce is warm.
Taste before adding salt; the cheese is salty.
Ask for extra pepper if you like more heat.
pairing: Sparkling water or a crisp white wine cuts through the salty cheese.

taste_bridges.indian: Peppery and cheesy, like a dry curry’s pepper warmth, without the spice mix.

name: Bucatini all'amatriciana
description: A tomato sauce with cured pork cheek, pecorino and a little chilli, traditionally served with thick hollow bucatini.
familiarity_bridge: A tangy tomato sauce with smoky pork, cheese and a gentle chilli warmth.
verdict: Worth a try if you eat pork and enjoy tomato sauces.
acquired_taste: Familiar tomato flavors make it friendly, though bucatini takes practice to twirl.
how_to_eat: Twirl a few strands of bucatini at a time.
Use a spoon if the long pasta is tricky.
Avoid cutting pasta if you want to follow local table custom.

order_phrases.text: Senza carne di maiale, per favore

pairing: Bread helps with the tomato sauce; try a medium-bodied red wine.

name: Orecchiette con cime di rapa
description: Small ear-shaped pasta with bitter turnip greens, garlic, olive oil and often anchovy.
familiarity_bridge: The bitter greens may recall sarson ka saag, paired with garlic and anchovy instead of spices.
verdict: A rewarding choice if you enjoy leafy greens and bitter flavors.
acquired_taste: The bitterness is distinctive and can be surprising on a first bite.
how_to_eat: Scoop greens and pasta together in each bite.
Taste before adding salt; anchovy may season the dish.
Ask if anchovy is included if you avoid fish.
pairing: Bread and sparkling water work well with the bitter greens.

taste_bridges.indian: The bitter greens may recall sarson ka saag, paired with garlic and anchovy instead of spices.

name: Penne all'arrabbiata
description: Penne in a tomato, garlic and chilli sauce. The name means angry, referring to the heat.
familiarity_bridge: A straightforward tomato sauce with chilli heat; ask for less chilli if needed.
verdict: Good if you like spicy tomato dishes; choose another dish if chilli is a concern.
acquired_taste: Heat varies by kitchen; first-timers often underestimate the chilli.
how_to_eat: Take a small first bite to check the heat.
Use bread to ease chilli heat; water may not help much.
Ask for it mildly spicy when ordering.
pairing: Bread helps more than water; sparkling water or a mild red wine pairs well.
